original_question: Does every k-blocked point set have O(k^2) points?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Conjecture 4: the strong size conjecture for k-blocked point sets, namely that every k-blocked point set has at most k^2 points. The immediately following Conjecture 5 is the stronger neighboring statement that each colour class has size at most k.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main object studied here (k-blocked point sets) and the intended quadratic growth scale in k for the total number of points.
missing_details: The paper works with a finite point set P in the Euclidean plane.
A point x blocks two points v and w exactly when x lies in the interior of the segment vw.
The blocker in the definition must be some other point of P; external blockers are not part of the notion of a k-blocked point set.

A k-blocked point set is not just any coloured point set: each point of P is assigned one of k colours so that for every distinct v,w in P, v and w have the same colour if and only if some other point of P blocks v and w.
Visibility and blocking are taken with respect to the whole set P.
The nearest official formulation in the paper is exact, not asymptotic: it asks for the bound |P| <= k^2, not merely O(k^2).
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is for every integer k >= 1.
Nearby paper-faithful context includes Lemma 4 and Lemma 5: at most three points are collinear in a k-blocked point set, and each colour class is in general position.
The immediately adjacent Conjecture 5 is stronger: each colour class has at most k points, which would imply the k^2 total-size bound.
refined_question: For every integer k >= 1, if P is a finite set of points in the plane and each point of P is assigned one of k colours so that for every distinct v,w in P, the points v and w receive the same colour if and only if some third point of P lies in the interior of the segment vw, must |P| <= k^2?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the strong quadratic-size conjecture in the blocked-point-set subsection, not the broader bounded-size conjecture. In Section 2.4 the paper first introduces k-blocked point sets and states Conjecture 3, which only asks for some bound depending on k. It then immediately records the sharper Conjecture 4, whose intent is the exact quadratic upper bound, followed by the even stronger Conjecture 5 that each colour class has at most k points. So the paper-faithful refinement should use the exact k^2 bound and should spell out the definition of a k-blocked point set from the surrounding context, rather than the weaker asymptotic O(k^2) phrasing.
